title: Tenant Geo-Lock and Affinity Controls for Hosted API
creator: Asha Patel
description: Provide a tenant-level feature that lets customers lock their Hosted API traffic and persisted artifacts to a configured set of geographic regions (primary + optional affinity set), expose Console and API controls for configuring geo-lock and retention overrides, and produce cryptographically verifiable evidence bundles for audits. The goal is to offer a strong compliance primitive for customers with regulatory or contractual residency requirements while preserving runtime availability through configurable, documented fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Console: admin flow to set tenant geo-lock with list of allowed regions and optional affinity weights; save and audit log user and timestamp.
API: public admin endpoint to set/get tenant geo-lock and retention override (RBAC-protected); returns current policy and history.

Serving: routing layer honours tenant geo-lock and attempts to serve requests from allowed regions; if capacity unavailable, follows explicit fallback policy (deny | queued-burst | failover-to-secondary-region) per tenant config.
Storage: persisted artifacts (logs, request traces, cached KV) tagged with residency metadata and stored only in allowed regions for locked tenants.
Retention Overrides: admin can set shorter/longer retention for logs and embeddings for a tenant; enforcement job purges data and produces evidence of deletion.

Evidence Automation: support one-click export that bundles provenance metadata, list of data locations, S3/ARC manifests, and signed timestamp; export artifact format documented and downloadable from Console and via API.
Metrics & Alerts: dashboards show number of geo-locked tenants, per-region capacity conflicts, and number of policy violations; create alert when a geo-locked tenant experiences a forced failover.
Security Review: design and implementation pass security review and threat modelling, including key handling for signed evidence exports.
Migration: existing tenants default to no-lock; admin migration tool exists to bulk-tag tenants and preview capacity impact before enabling lock.
notes: Tradeoffs: strict geo-lock (deny outside allowed regions) provides the strongest compliance guarantee but increases outage risk. We will expose two enforcement modes: strict and soft (log-and-allow with telemetry) to let customers validate before hard cutover.

Routing approach: prefer region-localized routing using residency-aware service discovery + affinity weights. Kernel: routing policy enforced at edge proxy and verified at serving runtime using residency metadata on each request.
Storage implications: some system-level logs currently aggregated across regions; we must introduce per-tenant partitioning or selective export to meet lock requirements.
Cost: customers selecting many allowed regions will increase egress/storage costs. Console should display estimated monthly cost delta when editing geo-lock.
Rollout plan: gated beta for enterprise customers (opt-in) -> broader GA after 8-week beta and at least two audit exports reviewed by legal teams.

Open questions: how to treat cross-region model cache (KV cache) when locked; propose a KV replication policy that only replicates to allowed regions or keeps cold backup outside allowed regions with encrypted wrap keys controlled by customer (follow-up with Security).
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Decided to support both Console UI and admin API for policy management to satisfy automation and SSO use-cases.
2025-02-20: Chosen evidence export format: signed ZIP containing manifest.json, per-region location map, and SHA256 digests. Proof-of-deletion to include deletion logs and storage provider receipts.
2025-02-24: Opted for soft-enforce rollout toggle: initially mark violations as incidents; hard enforcement delayed until customers validate.
2025-02-26: Agreed to include cost-estimation widget in Console when toggling geo-lock.
2025-02-27: Security requested HSM-backed signing for evidence exports; added to security review scope.
